standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence of geometric regularity of the fibre, formal smoothness of the fibre, and formal smoothness of the local map
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Theorem \ref{theorem-regular-fs}, cited at proof lines 10096 and again at 10198 and 10241
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence of (1) and (2), and supplies the final lifting argument used to finish (2) implies (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Formal smoothness of a local homomorphism implies flatness
standard_prerequisites.use: Yields flatness of A to B from condition (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change of formal smoothness, and preservation of formal smoothness under completion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-base-change-fs} and Lemma \ref{lemma-formally-smooth-completion}, cited at proof lines 10100, 10104, and 10150
standard_prerequisites.use: Transport the hypothesis to the special fibre and let the author replace A and B by their completions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of the diagram of Noetherian complete local rings S over R mapping to B over A
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-embed-map-Noetherian-complete-local-rings}, cited at proof lines 10112 and 10143
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the power series model of the extension that the reduction to equal special fibres works with.

standard_prerequisites.name: The quotient of a power series ring by part of a regular system of parameters is again a power series ring over a field or a Cohen ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen}, cited at proof lines 10135 and 10165
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies S after the cut as a power series ring, which is what makes the universal property argument available.

core_obligations: Show (1) implies (2) by quoting the regular-fibre theorem (proof lines 10096-10097).
Assume (3) and deduce (2): flatness from formal smoothness of the local map, and formal smoothness of k to the special fibre by base change (proof lines 10098-10102).
Assume (2) and reduce to A and B Noetherian complete local, using that both formal smoothness and flatness survive completion (proof lines 10103-10110).

Choose the diagram S over R mapping to B over A and cut J down by a regular sequence lifted from the special fibre so that the special fibres of S and B agree; conclude that S tensor A over R equals B, and reduce to formal smoothness of R to S (proof lines 10111-10150).

Present S as a power series ring over a coefficient field or a Cohen ring and run the lifting argument: filter the square-zero ideal, reduce to the case of a vector space, adjust the lift by a derivation into that ideal, and use injectivity of the differentials of the residue field extension to finish (proof lines 10151-10249).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the single substantive implication (2) implies (3) (proof lines 10096-10102).
Pass to completions and choose the Cohen-ring diagram (proof lines 10103-10121).
Kill a regular sequence to make the special fibres equal (proof lines 10122-10150).
Model S as a power series ring and reduce the lifting problem to a square-zero ideal annihilated by the maximal ideal (proof lines 10151-10192).
Solve the reduced lifting problem using derivations and differentials (proof lines 10193-10249).
difficulty_reason: The proposition proves the equivalence of three conditions on a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings: flatness together with geometric regularity of the special fibre, flatness together with formal smoothness of the fibre in the maximal-adic topology, and formal smoothness of the local map itself. One equivalence is quoted from the regular-fibre theorem and one implication follows from flatness of formally smooth maps plus base change, so the substance is the remaining implication: the author first replaces the rings by their completions, then chooses the standard diagram of a power series ring over a Cohen ring mapping to the target, cuts the target down by a regular sequence so that the special fibres become equal, and finishes with the lifting argument of the regular-fibre theorem in which a derivation into a square-zero ideal is adjusted by a map on differentials. The proof is a long, self-contained chain of reductions and is fully displayed.
